title: Infostealer riding the AI Train
description: Aokigahara is a newly observed infostealer malware that targets a wide range of sensitive data on Windows systems. It steals traditional credentials such as browser passwords, cookies, cryptocurrency wallets, VPN and FTP client data, email profiles, and password manager files. Uniquely, it also targets AI applications and developer tools including Claude, ChatGPT Desktop, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot, and Gemini CLI, collecting authentication files, session tokens, and configuration data. The malware additionally targets cloud environment credentials for AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud, as well as developer environment secrets like Git credentials and SSH private keys. Stolen AI and cloud credentials could enable unauthorized access to paid AI services, cloud resources, and source code repositories. The malware includes capabilities such as screenshot capture, clipboard theft, and a clipper component for cryptocurrency manipulation. There is no confirmed information on how the stolen data is monetized. No patch or remediation guidance is provided.
aiSummary: Aokigahara is an infostealer malware observed in the wild that combines traditional data theft capabilities with dedicated routines targeting AI applications, developer tools, and cloud environments. It collects browser credentials and cookies from Chromium-based and Firefox browsers, desktop and browser cryptocurrency wallets, messaging and gaming platform tokens, VPN and FTP client configurations, email profiles, and password manager data. Its distinctive feature is the aisessions handler that targets authentication and session data for AI tools such as Claude, ChatGPT Desktop, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot, and Gemini CLI, as well as cloud credentials for AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud. The ide handler collects local development environment secrets including Git credentials and SSH keys. The malware also captures system information, screenshots, clipboard contents, and deploys a clipper component for clipboard manipulation. The scope of stolen data reflects a shift toward targeting AI services and developer environments, potentially enabling unauthorized access to paid AI accounts, cloud resources, and source code repositories. The analysis does not confirm exploitation or monetization methods. No patch or vendor advisory is available.
aiImpact: The malware enables attackers to steal a broad range of sensitive information including authentication credentials, session tokens, and configuration files for browsers, cryptocurrency wallets, messaging apps, gaming platforms, VPN and FTP clients, email applications, password managers, AI development tools, and cloud environments. This can lead to unauthorized access to personal accounts, paid AI services, cloud resources, and developer repositories. The theft of AI-related credentials and cloud secrets could facilitate account takeover, data exfiltration, and misuse of paid AI services or cloud infrastructure. The presence of a clipper component also suggests potential financial theft via cryptocurrency manipulation. However, the exact impact depends on how attackers leverage the stolen data, which is not confirmed.
